12-01.t: Birth of G-Protein Discoverer Martin Rodbell
12-01.s: American biochemist and molecular endocrinologist Martin Rodbell was born in Baltimore. He shared the 1994 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering G-proteins and their role in cellular signal transduction.

12-01.t: First Global Observance of World AIDS Day
12-01.s: Designated by the World Health Organization and supported by the United Nations, the first World AIDS Day was observed worldwide under the theme 'Join the Worldwide Effort' to raise awareness and combat stigma.

12-02.t: Birth of Anemia Pioneer George Richards Minot
12-02.s: American physician George Richards Minot was born in Boston. He shared the 1934 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that liver therapy effectively treats pernicious anemia.
The Pan American Sanitary Bureau (precursor to the Pan American Health Organization) was established, marking the start of formal international public health cooperation in the Americas.

12-03.t: First Recorded Successful Separation of Conjoined Twins
12-03.s: Swiss surgeon Johannes Fatio completed the first documented successful separation of conjoined twins (Elizabeth and Catherine Meyerin) in Basel using a staged ligature technique over nine days.
South African cardiac surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the world's first successful human heart transplant on patient Louis Washkansky at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.

12-04.t: Oral Contraceptive Pill Made Available on Britain's NHS
12-04.s: The female oral contraceptive pill became available through the National Health Service in Great Britain, transforming reproductive medicine and family planning.

12-04.t: First Birth After Deceased-Donor Uterus Transplant
12-04.s: Physicians in São Paulo, Brazil, reported the world's first successful live birth resulting from a uterus transplanted from a deceased donor.

12-05.t: Birth of Glycogen Metabolism Pioneer Carl Ferdinand Cori
12-05.s: Czech-American biochemist and pharmacologist Carl Ferdinand Cori was born in Prague. Together with his wife Gerty Cori, he won the 1947 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the catalytic conversion of glycogen (the Cori cycle).

12-06.t: First Human Heart Transplant in the United States
12-06.s: Cardiac surgeon Adrian Kantrowitz performed the first human heart transplant in the United States at Maimonides Medical Center in Brooklyn, New York, on a newborn infant with Ebstein anomaly.

12-07.t: Birth of Cell Theory Co-Founder Theodor Schwann
12-07.s: German physiologist Theodor Schwann was born in Neuss. He co-founded cell theory, discovered the digestive enzyme pepsin, and identified the myelin-producing Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system.
Austrian ophthalmologist Eduard Zirm performed the world's first successful full-thickness human corneal transplant (keratoplasty), restoring partial vision to a man blinded by lime burns.

12-09.t: Birth of Dr. Ida Sophia Scudder, Founder of CMC Vellore
12-09.s: Born in Ranipet, India, Dr. Ida Scudder dedicated her life to women's healthcare and medical education in India, founding the Christian Medical College and Hospital in Vellore in 1918.
An international commission of scientists certified that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, making it the first human infectious disease eliminated through coordinated global vaccination.

12-09.t: First Nationwide National Immunization Day (Pulse Polio) in India
12-09.s: The Government of India conducted its first nationwide National Immunization Day for poliomyelitis eradication, vaccinating approximately 87 million children under three years of age.

12-10.t: First Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine Awarded
12-10.s: German physiologist Emil von Behring received the inaugural Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm for his work on serum therapy, particularly its application against diphtheria.

12-10.t: Sir Ronald Ross Receives the Nobel Prize for Malaria Discovery in India
12-10.s: Indian Medical Service officer Ronald Ross received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm for demonstrating that Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria, a breakthrough achieved during his work in Secunderabad and Calcutta.

12-10.t: Watson, Crick, and Wilkins Receive Nobel Prize for DNA Structure
12-10.s: Francis Crick, James Watson, and Maurice Wilkins were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm for discovering the molecular double-helix structure of DNA.

12-10.t: Har Gobind Khorana Receives the Nobel Prize for Deciphering the Genetic Code
12-10.s: Indian-born biochemist Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm alongside Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg for interpreting the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis.

12-11.t: Birth of Bacteriology Founder Robert Koch
12-11.s: German physician and microbiologist Robert Koch was born in Clausthal. He identified the causative bacteria of anthrax, tuberculosis, and cholera, formulated Koch's postulates, and won the 1905 Nobel Prize.

12-11.t: FDA Issues First EUA for a COVID-19 Vaccine (Pfizer-BioNTech)
12-11.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued its first Emergency Use Authorization for a COVID-19 vaccine, authorizing the Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine for individuals ages 16 and older.

12-12.t: Emil von Behring Delivers First Medicine Nobel Lecture
12-12.s: Emil von Behring delivered his Nobel Lecture 'Serum Therapy in Therapeutics and Medical Science' in Stockholm, outlining the immunological principles behind passive immunization.

12-13.t: Claude Beck Publishes First Human Open-Chest Defibrillation
12-13.s: Cardiac surgeon Claude Schaeffer Beck published in JAMA the first report of successful open-chest electrical defibrillation in a human, reversing prolonged ventricular fibrillation in a 14-year-old boy.

12-14.s: American geneticist Edward Lawrie Tatum was born in Boulder, Colorado. He shared the 1958 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for showing that genes act by regulating specific chemical events ('one gene, one enzyme').

12-14.t: First Public COVID-19 Vaccine Administered in the United States
12-14.s: New York intensive care nurse Sandra Lindsay became the first person in the United States outside of clinical trials to receive an authorized COVID-19 vaccine.

12-15.t: Birth of Phototherapy Pioneer Niels Ryberg Finsen
12-15.s: Faroese-Danish physician Niels Ryberg Finsen was born in Tórshavn. He received the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing concentrated light radiation therapy (phototherapy) to treat lupus vulgaris.

12-15.t: APA Removes Homosexuality from List of Mental Disorders
12-15.s: The American Psychiatric Association voted to remove homosexuality from its Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM), marking a landmark shift in psychiatric medicine.

12-16.t: UK National Insurance Act Becomes Law
12-16.s: The United Kingdom's National Insurance Act of 1911 became law, establishing compulsory health insurance for millions of British industrial workers and laying the foundation for national healthcare.

12-18.t: Birth of Oncogene Pioneer Harold E. Varmus
12-18.s: American physician-scientist Harold E. Varmus was born in Oceanside, New York. He shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the cellular origin of retroviral oncogenes and later served as NIH Director.

12-18.t: FDA Grants EUA for Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine
12-18.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization for Moderna's mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, co-developed with scientists at the NIH National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.

12-19.t: Birth of Sir Upendranath Brahmachari, Discoverer of Urea Stibamine
12-19.s: Born in Sardanga, West Bengal, physician and scientist Sir Upendranath Brahmachari synthesized urea stibamine in 1922, providing the first effective cure for kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) and saving millions of lives.

12-20.t: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) Founded in Paris
12-20.s: Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) was founded in Paris by French physicians and journalists to provide independent emergency medical aid in conflict and disaster zones.

12-21.t: FDA Approves First Long-Acting Injectable HIV PrEP
12-21.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved cabotegravir extended-release injectable suspension (Apretude), the first long-acting injectable medication for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis administered every two months.

12-22.t: Birth of BCG Vaccine Co-Developer Camille Guérin
12-22.s: French veterinarian and bacteriologist Camille Guérin was born in Poitiers. Working with Albert Calmette, he developed the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine against tuberculosis.

12-22.t: FDA Authorizes First Oral Antiviral Pill for COVID-19 (Paxlovid)
12-22.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Emergency Use Authorization for Pfizer's Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir), the first at-home oral antiviral treatment for high-risk COVID-19 patients.

12-23.t: First Successful Human Kidney Transplant Performed
12-23.s: Surgeon Dr. Joseph E. Murray performed the world's first successful human kidney transplant between identical twins at Peter Bent Brigham Hospital in Boston, launching modern organ transplantation and earning the 1990 Nobel Prize.

12-23.t: National Cancer Act of 1971 Signed into Law
12-23.s: President Richard Nixon signed the National Cancer Act of 1971, launching the modern U.S. National Cancer Program and establishing comprehensive cancer centers and expanded federal oncology research.

12-24.t: Birth of Immunologist and Public Health Leader Anthony Fauci
12-24.s: American physician-scientist Anthony S. Fauci was born in Brooklyn, New York. As long-serving director of NIAID, he pioneered vasculitis therapy and led U.S. biomedical responses to HIV/AIDS, Ebola, and COVID-19.

12-25.t: Birth of Cancer Pathologist James Stephen Ewing
12-25.s: American pathologist James Stephen Ewing was born in Pittsburgh. A pioneer in oncology and founder of the American Association for Cancer Research, he first described the malignant bone tumor known as Ewing sarcoma in 1921.

12-25.t: Birth of Electron Microscope Inventor Ernst Ruska
12-25.s: German physicist Ernst Ruska was born in Heidelberg. His invention of the electron microscope (1986 Nobel Prize) enabled direct visualization of viruses, organelles, and ultrastructural pathology.

12-25.t: Launch of Mission Indradhanush Immunization Drive
12-25.s: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched Mission Indradhanush as a targeted catch-up vaccination campaign under the Universal Immunization Programme to achieve at least 90% full immunization coverage among children and pregnant women.

12-26.t: Marie and Pierre Curie Announce Discovery of Radium
12-26.s: Marie and Pierre Curie announced the isolation of radium to the French Academy of Sciences, laying the scientific foundation for brachytherapy and modern radiation oncology.

12-26.t: Birth of Dr. Sushila Nayyar, Union Health Minister and Founder of MGIMS
12-26.s: Born in Kunjah, Punjab, Lady Hardinge Medical College alumna Dr. Sushila Nayyar served as Mahatma Gandhi's personal physician, twice as India's Health Minister, and founded the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS) in Sevagram in 1969.

12-26.t: National Eye Institute Established at NIH
12-26.s: The National Eye Institute was formally established at the National Institutes of Health to lead federal biomedical research into vision disorders and blindness.

12-27.t: Birth of Microbiology Pioneer Louis Pasteur
12-27.s: French chemist and microbiologist Louis Pasteur was born in Dole. His breakthroughs in germ theory, pasteurization, and vaccines for anthrax and rabies revolutionized infectious disease medicine.

12-27.t: First Use of Ether Anesthesia for Childbirth
12-27.s: American physician Dr. Crawford Williamson Long administered diethyl ether anesthesia during childbirth for the first time in Jefferson, Georgia, delivering his own child painlessly.

The All India Institute of Mental Health (est. 1954) and the Mysore State Mental Hospital were amalgamated to form the autonomous National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS) in Bengaluru.

12-28.s: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen submitted his landmark paper 'On a New Kind of Rays' detailing the discovery of X-rays, inaugurating modern diagnostic medical imaging.

12-28.t: Founding of the Indian Medical Association (IMA)
12-28.s: At the 5th All India Medical Conference in Calcutta under the presidency of Dr. G. V. Deshmukh, Indian doctors passed a resolution establishing the All India Medical Association, renamed the Indian Medical Association in 1930.

12-28.t: First American IVF Baby Born in Virginia
12-28.s: Elizabeth Jordan Carr, the first baby conceived through in vitro fertilization (IVF) in the United States, was born in Norfolk, Virginia, advancing reproductive endocrinology.

12-28.t: DCGI Approves Indigenous COVID-19 Vaccine Corbevax
12-28.s: The Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) granted restricted emergency use approval for Biological E's protein subunit COVID-19 vaccine Corbevax among adults.

12-30.t: Inauguration of the All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health (AIIH&PH)
12-30.s: Established in Kolkata with assistance from the Rockefeller Foundation, the All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health was inaugurated as India's pioneering institution for public health research and training.
The United Kingdom granted emergency use authorization to the Oxford University-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, enabling rapid rollout of a refrigerator-stable viral vector vaccine.

12-31.t: Birth of Modern Anatomy Founder Andreas Vesalius
12-31.s: Flemish anatomist and physician Andreas Vesalius was born in Brussels. His 1543 masterwork 'De humani corporis fabrica' overturned centuries of Galenic dogma and established modern human anatomy based on direct dissection.
